questionText:
Let $\oplus$ and $\odot$ denote the Exclusive OR and Exclusive NOR operations, respectively.

Which one of the following is NOT CORRECT?
explanation:
Let us analyze each option one by one:

Option (A): $\overline{P \oplus Q} = P \odot Q$
The complement of XOR is XNOR. Thus, $\overline{P \oplus Q} = P \odot Q$. This statement is CORRECT.

Option (B): $\bar{P} \oplus Q = P \odot Q$
Complementing exactly one input of an XOR operation turns it into an XNOR operation. Thus, $\bar{P} \oplus Q = P \odot Q$. This statement is CORRECT.

Option (C): $\bar{P} \oplus \bar{Q} = P \oplus Q$
Complementing both inputs of an XOR operation leaves the function unchanged. Thus, $\bar{P} \oplus \bar{Q} = P \oplus Q$. This statement is CORRECT.

Option (D): $(P \oplus \bar{P}) \oplus Q = (P \odot \bar{P}) \odot \bar{Q}$
• LHS: $P \oplus \bar{P} = 1$, so $(1) \oplus Q = \bar{Q}$.
• RHS: $P \odot \bar{P} = 0$, so $(0) \odot \bar{Q} = \overline{0 \oplus \bar{Q}} = \overline{\bar{Q}} = Q$.
Since $\bar{Q} \neq Q$, LHS $\neq$ RHS. Therefore, this statement is NOT CORRECT.
